title: Barack Obama Surprises WNBA All-Stars at Presidential Center Practice
excerpt: The former president walked onto the court before Friday's practice in Chicago, praising players for elevating women's basketball and chatting with Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese.
body:
• Former President Barack Obama made a surprise appearance at WNBA All-Star practice on Friday at his newly opened Presidential Center in Chicago.
  • Obama addressed the 22 All-Stars, praised the growth of women's basketball, and spent about 10 minutes taking photos with players.
  • Caitlin Clark said Obama bonded with her over navigating media scrutiny, telling her he "got famous in my 40s, I didn't have to do it in my 20s."
  • The All-Star Game takes place Saturday at the United Center. Obama said he will not attend due to a prior commitment.

Former President Barack Obama surprised WNBA All-Stars at their practice on Friday morning, walking through a side door at the newly opened Obama Presidential Center in Chicago to address the league's 22 best players.

"This doesn't look like the toughest practice I've ever seen," Obama said with a laugh, according to USA Today. "But it's All-Star break, y'all aren't supposed to be working too hard. Though I suspect it may get a little competitive toward the end of the game."

A Presidential Pep Talk

Obama spoke to the group for several minutes, acknowledging both familiar faces and first-time meetings. "Some of you I'm meeting for the first time, all of you are extraordinary," he said, according to NBC Sports. "The way the game has been growing lately and the way the game has been picking up — people have been paying attention to your excellence. It has been a sight to see."

https://x.com/SInow/status/2080670059098145074

After a group photo, the former president spent about 10 minutes shaking hands and posing for individual pictures. He gave a shout-out to Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson before chatting with her one-on-one.

"When I got famous in my 40s, I didn't have to do it in my 20s."

— Barack Obama to Caitlin Clark, on navigating media scrutiny

Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark said her conversation with Obama was "a moment I'll probably remember for the rest of my life." The two bonded over handling intense public attention, with Obama reminding the 24-year-old that he faced that pressure at a later stage in life.

"Sometimes, I think, people don't always realize, like, I'm 24 years old and I'm trying to navigate a lot of different things while trying to play basketball at the same time," Clark told reporters. "It was cool to hear that from him and I think, honestly, it's probably a good reminder for all of us to treat people with respect, treat people with grace."

Selfies and One-on-One

Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese, a former Chicago Sky player, made sure to capture the moment. "I got my selfie," Reese told reporters with a smile. "Not everybody just gets to meet Barack Obama. That was my first time too."

Obama also briefly squared up with New York Liberty center Jonquel Jones, getting into a defensive stance on the court for a few seconds. He told players he no longer plays five-on-five to protect his Achilles tendon, but said he had broken in the Presidential Center's regulation-size court with a game of horse.

The former president was given an autographed blue No. 44 WNBA All-Star jersey. Dallas Wings guard Paige Bueckers and Las Vegas Aces coach Becky Hammon were among others who spoke with Obama individually.

All-Star Weekend at the Obama Center

The WNBA is the first professional sports league to use the nearly 20-acre Obama Presidential Center campus in Jackson Park. The center, which features a regulation-size WNBA court labeled "Home Court," is hosting media day, practice, Changemaker Day, and Jr. WNBA Day on Friday. The 3-Point Contest takes place Friday evening at Wintrust Arena, and the All-Star Game is Saturday at the United Center.

Obama told the players he would not be able to attend the game due to a previous engagement. Former First Lady Michelle Obama was not present at Friday's practice.
